Q: Excel VBA file copy external to excel A:

One quick solution for you is to keep Excel responsive. It can be done by adding an instruction DoEvents to your code. Here is a code example that prints to the immediate output window a range of strings like "C:\User\N\abc.txt" where N is 1 to 10000 (just for the sake of example, A1 and A2 cells contain strings "User" and "abc.txt").

Sub so_vba()

For j = 1 To 1e4
  Strng = "C:\" & Cells(1, 1).Value & "\" & Trim(Str(j)) & "\" & Cells(1, 2).Value
  Debug.Print Strng
  DoEvents
Next

End Sub

Without DoEvents this sub freezes my Excel for about 12 seconds.

Q: RangeError: WebAssembly.Instance(): Out of memory: wasm memory A:

I discussed this with my hosting support team. In my case, the root cause was a cPanel/CloudLinux memory limit affecting the Git deployment process.

I’m running a Laravel + Vite build on a dedicated server using cPanel Git Deploy and Node.js 22. Increasing the Max cPanel process memory resolved the WebAssembly.instantiate(): Out of memory error during the build.

Q: Handshake fails with RST after destination address modification of TCP packets in Netfilter hooks A:

You forgot to modify the source address of the return packet in the "received from the relay" case.

And I think you also forgot that Netfilter/conntrack is a separate entity from the TCP connect code – the TCP code doesn't use conntrack and doesn't know what Netfilter has done to its packets.

In other words, the "destination address is modified to 10.10.10.5" is happening after the TCP/IP socket code has already generated the packet and sent it off. This means that the original destination as known to the socket code (TCP/IP stack) is still something else, not 10.10.10.5. Even though Netfilter now expects 10.10.10.5, the TCP socket code doesn't know about any of that and still expects packets only from the original address that was supplied to the connect() call.

And since there is no socket connected to 10.10.10.5, the inbound SYN/ACK is correctly rejected as unknown.

When stateful DNAT is performed using the standard conntrack-based iptables/nft mechanisms, inbound reply packets are also automatically reverse-SNATed according to information stored in the conntrack state, so this problem doesn't occur.

(This hopefully also explains why Netfilter's existing DNAT is stateful and why you cannot really implement stateless 'many:1' NAT. Implementing 1:1 NAT would be possible, i.e. if your check had been if (iph->daddr == OTHER_HOST) then on ingress you could simply set the address back to OTHER_HOST – but as you're currently NATing everything that != the relay, you need some way to remember what the original address was, i.e. to keep state, i.e. reinvent conntrack.)

Q: Reshaping a table with multiple header rows within excel to place them horizontally as new columns A:

Before you promote headers in your tables, remove columns with all nulls (e.g. using Table.Profile) and then combine tables with Table.Combine.

let
    fx_select = (tbl) => Table.SelectColumns(
        tbl,
        List.RemoveLastN(
            Table.SelectRows(
                Table.Buffer(Table.Profile(tbl)), 
                (x) => x[Count] <> x[NullCount]
            )[Column], 
            1
        )
    ),
    Source = Excel.CurrentWorkbook(){[Name="data"]}[Content],
    last_column = List.Last(Table.ColumnNames(Source)),
    group = Table.Group(Source, last_column, {"x", (x) => Table.PromoteHeaders(fx_select(x))}),
    z = Table.Combine(group[x])
in
    z

Reorder columns after this.

Q: how to get mailbox size in exchange 2010 database A: 
Get-MailboxStatistics -Database 'Mailbox Database 123' |
Where-Object {$_.TotalItemSize.Value.ToMB() -le 5} |
Sort-Object TotalItemSize -Descending |
Select-Object DisplayName,TotalItemSize

Q: Should I change RSA algorithm to some more modern algorithm or just stay on RSA but use larger key length? A:

What secrets are you handling that must be kept that secure for so long? Only first world government's security services will be able to afford high end quantum computers that could crack the prime factorisation problem (iff they can ever be made to work at that sort of bit length).

Q: Getting "None of the following candidates is applicable" when trying to use LiveData list in itemsIndexed in LazyColumn A:

By calling observeAsState you convert the LiveData into a Compose State object. So the type of foods is State<List<Food>>. The itemsIndexed function expects a List, though, not a List wrapped in a State. You need to unwrap the State first.

That's simple:

  • Either access the value of the State instead of the State itself:

    itemsIndexed(foods.value)

  • Or let Kotlin unwrap the State for you automatically, by using delegation:

    val foods by foodViewModel.allFoods.observeAsState(listOf())

    Then you can keep using itemsIndexed(foods) { index, food -> }, because foods is now just a simple List.

Just make sure you use the correct import statement, not the one from your question:

import androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.itemsIndexed

That said, you should remove LiveData from your app entirely. LiveData is a relic of earlier times that also worked in Java, where you don't have Flows. Especially when using Compose with the State mechanic, using LiveData is very anachronistic.

The asLiveData function you use on your repository Flow is only useful to bridge legacay code, i.e. when you still have an old Java-based UI but already started migrating your data sources to Kotlin. But you use a modern Compose UI, so no need to hassle with LiveData and its limitations.

Instead, just purge LiveData from your app and replace the view model's allFoods property with this:

val allFoods: StateFlow<List<Food>> = repository.allFoods.stateIn(
    scope = viewModelScope,
    started = SharingStarted.WhileSubscribed(5.seconds),
    initialValue = emptyList(),
)

This converts the repository Flow into a StateFlow, a specially configured Flow that acts as an observable data holder, much like a Compose State (or the LiveData in your old code). It can then easily be converted into a State by using this in your composables:

val foods by foodViewModel.allFoods.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()

That's it, foods is now a List<Food> again and the rest of your app works unaffected.

Using Flows consistently throughout your app is more performant than using LiveData because the consumer (your UI) can control the producer (your database or whatever) to stop producing values when the UI doesn't need them (e.g. the user navigated to another screen, or the app was sent to the background, and so on).
